summary: Vice President JD Vance has become an unexpected focal point in the disclosure conversation this week, publicly stating his obsession with accessing UFO files while characterizing extraterrestrials as "demons" – a theological framing that prompted Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb to offer a direct rebuttal. Meanwhile, the 3I/ATLAS mystery deepens with new reporting of nuclear fuel signatures detected in connection with the object, adding a material dimension to ongoing speculation. A batch of archived UAP documents spanning from early 2024 through October have surfaced, providing additional data points for researchers tracking official encounters. The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act includes an estimated briefing deadline in late June, suggesting Congress will soon demand fresh intelligence on government UAP findings. With Contact in the Desert scheduled for May and continued documentary scrutiny of disclosure narratives, the conversation is actively shifting from whether information exists to what the public should understand about it.
